loanTypes.heading: Check your plot loan type first

list.heading: Different Loan Types–
list.desc: Plot loans can vary based on factors like location (urban vs. rural), purpose (investment vs. construction), and lender policies. Knowing the right type helps you choose the best financing option.

list.heading: Plot-Only Loan–
list.desc: A Plot-Only Loan is ideal if you're buying land without immediate construction plans. However, lenders may have restrictions on location, land type, and tenure.

list.heading: Plot + Construction Loan–
list.desc: A Plot + Construction Loan suits those planning to build soon. It often comes with better terms since it covers both land purchase and construction.

list.heading: Encroachment issues–
list.desc:
Local land mafia or neighbors may illegally occupy your land.
Fake documents may be created to claim ownership.

list.heading: Multiple buyers–
list.desc: Fraudsters may sell the same plot to multiple people using duplicate sale deeds.

list.heading: Hidden Liabilities–
list.desc:
Outstanding property tax, electricity bills, or other dues may transfer to the new owner.
Loan fraud—land sold despite being mortgaged to a bank.

list.heading: No proper possession–
list.desc:
Real estate developers may delay handing over possession after payment.
Some builders falsely claim land approvals and then abandon projects.

list.heading: Fake cooperative societies–
list.desc:
Some plots are sold in unauthorized layouts, leading to demolition by authorities.
Fraudulent cooperative housing societies sell land they don't own.

awareness.heading: Important steps before buying a plot

cards.heading: Verify title and ownership
cards.para: Ensure that the title deed is genuine and that the seller is the rightful owner by checking government records.

cards.heading: Confirm boundaries​​
cards.para: Check that the plot's boundaries are clearly marked and free from any encroachments.

cards.heading: Review documentation​
cards.para: Make sure all documents—such as sale deeds, land records, and approvals—are complete and authentic.

cards.heading: Check regulatory approvals
cards.para: Verify that the plot has the necessary clearances, including land use conversion and zoning permissions.​

cards.heading: Avoid double selling​
cards.para: Confirm that the plot isn't being sold to multiple buyers at the same time.

cards.heading: Choose reputable agents​
cards.para: Work with trusted brokers or developers to reduce the risk of misrepresentation or fraudulent practices.

thinkYouShouldKnow.heading: Things you should know
paraGraph: Independent Facilitator: DigitalDSA operates as an independent loan facilitator and web aggregator, bridging the gap between loan consumers and licensed banks or NBFCs. We are not an authorized financial institution and do not offer loans directly.

Loan Approval: The sole discretion of approving or rejecting a loan lies with the respective bank or NBFC where the user applies. DigitalDSA does not guarantee loan approval or offer assurance from any specific bank or NBFC. All loans are subject to credit approval, and their terms, conditions, fees, and charges apply.
Liability: DigitalDSA is not responsible for any loss, damage, or failure at the user's end during loan processing. The final decision of the bank or NBFC is binding on both the user and DigitalDSA.

Important Information: This information is provided without considering your personal objectives, financial situation, or needs. Please assess its suitability before acting. Exclusive offers are available only when you avail of a loan through DigitalDSA and meet specific conditions.
